title: How a Power Bank Works in 60 Seconds 🔋⚡ #shorts
description:
A power bank stores energy in lithium-ion cells at about 3.7 volts, then a boost converter steps it up to 5 volts for USB. That conversion loses some energy, so a 10,000 mAh power bank usually delivers only about 6,000 to 7,000 mAh to your phone. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#powerbank #battery #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A *10,000 mAh* power bank can't actually give your phone 10,000 mAh.

steps.label: Cells
steps.text: Inside are *lithium-ion cells* that store energy at about *3.7 volts*.

steps.label: Charging
steps.text: When you plug it in, lithium ions move into the *graphite* side, storing energy.

steps.label: Boost
steps.text: USB needs *5 volts*, so a *boost converter* steps the voltage up.

steps.label: Losses
steps.text: Higher voltage and some *heat loss* mean only about *60–70%* reaches your phone.

steps.label: Protection
steps.text: A *protection chip* stops overcharging, overheating and short circuits.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Store, boost, *charge*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
